subject.title: [Feature Request] Telegram inline buttons for pairing approve/deny

question: Should Telegram chat callbacks be allowed to approve or deny pairing/device requests, and which operator scopes must a button press prove for DM pairing versus `operator.admin` browser/device approval?
rationale: The requested UX moves access-changing approval from explicit CLI or scoped gateway clients into Telegram callback handling, and current source intentionally gives Telegram command owners only `operator.pairing` for device-pair approvals.

options.title: Design typed pairing approval actions
options.body: Define reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use semantics, caller identity, audit, and existing scope enforcement before Telegram renders Approve/Deny buttons.

options.title: Limit first pass to DM pairing
options.body: Add buttons only for low-scope channel DM pairing and keep `operator.admin` browser/device approvals on CLI or Control UI until a separate step-up model lands.

options.title: Defer chat-originated approvals
options.body: Keep the command-copy workflow until the broader channel-aware device approval and step-up authorization direction is settled.

recommendation.title: Design typed pairing approval actions
recommendation.body: Define reusable approval actions with request id, action, expiry, single-use semantics, caller identity, audit, and existing scope enforcement before Telegram renders Approve/Deny buttons.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant history spans shared pairing formatting, native approval UX, and recent pairing work, making this the clearest routing candidate for the security/product decision.
